ChatGPT is deepening its integration with Google Drive, allowing users to add Google Drive files to ChatGPT's database and edit documents directly within the chat interface. Here are the details.

ChatGPT expands Google Drive plugin integration

According to Adam Fry, ChatGPT's head of consumer products, who announced on X, subscribers to ChatGPT's paid plans can now add Google Drive files to the ChatGPT database.

Fry said this makes it "more convenient to ask ChatGPT questions about files," and added that users can click the "+" button on the left side of the input box and then select "Add from database."

Through this new integration, paid users can now open and even edit Google Drive files directly within the chat interface without switching to other windows. ChatGPT still offers the option to open files in the corresponding Google apps (such as Google Docs or Google Sheets).

When responding to users on X, Fry explained that ChatGPT edits the original file in Google Drive directly, rather than creating a copy of a static file based on the existing document.

In addition to the Google Drive integration, Fry also mentioned three other features launched on ChatGPT this week, the most important of which is a new quiz tool that allows users to ask ChatGPT to generate questions around a specific topic. ChatGPT generates interactive quizzes that include multiple-choice questions, navigation features between questions, and hint buttons.

Fry also mentioned ChatGPT's previously announced Yelp integration, through which users can make restaurant reservations and join waitlists; there is also a new feature for paid users that provides "premium recommendations" on the ChatGPT homepage.
